Core node type representing any JSON value (null, boolean, number, string, array, object, or raw). Forms intrusive doubly-linked lists for arrays/objects via next/prev and contains hierarchical child for arrays/objects. Fields store type flags, name (for object members), and value representations. Managed by cJSON API; allocate via creation/parse functions and free with cJSON_Delete unless flagged as references.
Custom allocator hooks structure supplying malloc and free function pointers used by cJSON when initialized with cJSON_InitHooks.

objects.definition: typedef struct esl_mutex esl_mutex_t;
objects.description: Opaque mutex handle for the ESL threading abstraction. The struct is forward-declared only; its internal layout is hidden and managed by the ESL API. Used with esl_mutex_create/destroy/lock/trylock/unlock. Details of the underlying platform mutex are unknown from this header.

objects.definition: typedef struct esl_thread esl_thread_t;
objects.description: Opaque thread handle for the ESL threading abstraction. The struct is forward-declared only; its internal layout is hidden. Threads are typically created in detached mode via esl_thread_create_detached or esl_thread_create_detached_ex. Other lifecycle and join semantics are not exposed here.

objects.definition: typedef void *(*esl_thread_function_t) (esl_thread_t *, void *);

Configuration file handle and parser state for the ESL config parser. Holds the FILE stream and parsing context such as current category/section, buffers, and line/counters. Constructed by user as a stack/heap object whose fields are initialized by esl_config_open_file; closed with esl_config_close_file; iterated with esl_config_next_pair. The struct is fully defined here; ownership of FILE* is managed by this API. Unknown details: semantics of lockto are not documented.

C++ wrapper around the ESL/Freeswitch event system. Manages an underlying esl_event_t, provides helpers to construct, serialize, query, and modify event headers/body, set priority, and iterate headers. Ownership semantics indicated by 'mine' (whether this instance owns and frees the wrapped esl_event_t). Private hp caches header iteration state. Details of esl_event_t/esl_event_header_t come from esl.h and are not defined here.

C++ wrapper for an ESL connection/handle to FreeSWITCH's Event Socket. Encapsulates an esl_handle_t, providing constructors for TCP host/port/user/password or an existing socket, and methods to send commands, API/bgapi calls, send/receive events, manage filters and event subscriptions, execute apps (sync/async), and manage connection state. Actual transport and handle details are defined in esl.h.

functions.name: esl_vasprintf
functions.signature: int esl_vasprintf(char **ret, const char *fmt, va_list ap);
functions.description: Formats a string using a va_list and allocates the resulting buffer, similar to POSIX vasprintf. The formatted, NUL-terminated string is written to *ret on success.
requirements: ret must be a valid non-NULL pointer to a char*; on success, *ret will point to a heap-allocated buffer that the caller must free.
fmt must be a non-NULL format string compatible with printf-style formatting.
ap must be an initialized va_list corresponding to fmt.

functions.name: esl_global_set_logger
functions.description: Sets the global logger callback for libesl. By default, a null logger is used; this allows applications to receive log messages from the library.
requirements: logger may be NULL to disable logging, or a valid function pointer with signature void (*)(const char *file, const char *func, int line, int level, const char *fmt, ...).
May be called at process initialization before other libesl functions to ensure logs are captured.

functions.name: esl_global_set_default_logger
functions.description: Sets the default log level used by libesl’s internal logger. Higher/lower numeric values map to defined ESL_LOG_LEVEL_* constants.
requirements: level should be one of the ESL_LOG_LEVEL_* constants (0..7) defined in this header.

functions.name: esl_url_encode
functions.signature: size_t esl_url_encode(const char *url, char *buf, size_t len);
functions.description: URL-encodes the input string into the provided buffer. Returns the number of bytes written (excluding the NUL).
requirements: url must be a non-NULL C-string to encode.
buf must be non-NULL and have capacity of at least len bytes.
len must be large enough to hold the encoded output plus a terminating NUL; otherwise output may be truncated.
Caller is responsible for checking the return value to detect truncation.

functions.name: esl_url_decode
functions.description: In-place URL-decodes the given string. Returns the same pointer for convenience.
requirements: s must be a non-NULL, writable, NUL-terminated C-string buffer.
Buffer s must have been sized to hold the decoded data in place (decoding never expands length).

functions.name: esl_stristr
functions.description: Case-insensitive substring search. Returns a pointer to the first occurrence of str in instr, or NULL if not found.
requirements: instr must be a non-NULL C-string to search within.
str must be a non-NULL C-string to search for.

functions.name: esl_toupper
functions.description: Converts a character code to uppercase, similar to standard toupper, using libesl’s implementation.
requirements: c should be representable as an unsigned char cast or EOF (standard ctype-style expectation).

functions.name: esl_tolower
functions.description: Converts a character code to lowercase, similar to standard tolower, using libesl’s implementation.
requirements: c should be representable as an unsigned char cast or EOF (standard ctype-style expectation).

functions.name: esl_snprintf
functions.signature: int esl_snprintf(char *buffer, size_t count, const char *fmt, ...);
functions.description: Formats a string into buffer with size limit, similar to snprintf. Returns the number of characters that would have been written excluding the NUL terminator.
requirements: buffer must be a non-NULL writable buffer.
count is the size of buffer in bytes and should include space for the terminating NUL.
fmt must be a non-NULL format string; subsequent arguments must match the format specifiers.
Caller should check return value to detect truncation (return >= count).

functions.name: esl_attach_handle
functions.signature: esl_status_t esl_attach_handle(esl_handle_t *handle, esl_socket_t socket, struct sockaddr_in *addr);
functions.description: Attaches an esl_handle_t to an already-established socket connection, initializing the handle with connection details.
requirements: handle must be a valid, writable esl_handle_t pointer.
socket must be a valid, connected socket descriptor.
addr, if provided, should point to the connection’s sockaddr_in; may be used to populate the handle.
Must be called before performing I/O using the handle.

functions.name: esl_listen
functions.signature: esl_status_t esl_listen(const char *host, esl_port_t port, esl_listen_callback_t callback, void *user_data, esl_socket_t *server_sockP);
functions.description: Binds and listens on the specified host/port for outbound socket connections and invokes the callback for each accepted client.
requirements: host must be a valid local bind address or NULL/empty for INADDR_ANY (behavior depends on implementation).
port must be a valid TCP port number (>0).
callback must be a valid function pointer of type esl_listen_callback_t; it will be invoked per-connection.
server_sockP must be non-NULL; on success, *server_sockP receives the listening socket handle.
Caller is responsible for managing the lifecycle of the listening socket and any client sockets accepted by the callback.

functions.name: esl_listen_threaded
functions.signature: esl_status_t esl_listen_threaded(const char *host, esl_port_t port, esl_listen_callback_t callback, void *user_data, int max);
functions.description: Starts a threaded listener on host/port for outbound socket connections, dispatching accepted clients to the callback, with optional concurrency limit.
requirements: host must be a valid local bind address or NULL/empty for INADDR_ANY (behavior depends on implementation).
port must be a valid TCP port number (>0).
callback must be a valid function pointer of type esl_listen_callback_t; it will be invoked per-connection.
max should be a positive integer limiting concurrent handling (exact semantics depend on implementation).

functions.name: esl_execute
functions.signature: esl_status_t esl_execute(esl_handle_t *handle, const char *app, const char *arg, const char *uuid);
functions.description: Sends a sendmsg to execute an application (app) with an optional argument on a specific target UUID over an established ESL connection. Mainly for outbound socket use.
requirements: handle must refer to a connected and authenticated ESL session.
app must be a non-NULL application name recognized by the server.
arg may be NULL or a valid argument string, depending on the app.
uuid should be a valid session UUID if targeting a specific session; may be NULL to use a default target depending on server behavior.

functions.name: esl_sendevent
functions.description: Sends an event object over the ESL connection to the server.
requirements: handle must refer to a connected ESL session.
event must be a valid, properly constructed esl_event_t with required headers and body as expected by the server.

functions.name: esl_sendmsg
functions.description: Sends an event as a message (sendmsg-style) for the server to parse, optionally targeting a specific UUID.
requirements: handle must refer to a connected ESL session.
event must be a valid, properly constructed esl_event_t message.
uuid may be NULL to use the default target; otherwise must be a valid target UUID.

functions.name: esl_connect_timeout
functions.signature: esl_status_t esl_connect_timeout(esl_handle_t *handle, const char *host, esl_port_t port, const char *user, const char *password, uint32_t timeout);
functions.description: Connects an ESL handle to a host:port and authenticates with provided credentials. Includes a connection timeout in milliseconds.
requirements: handle must be a valid esl_handle_t pointer; it will be initialized/connected on success.
host must be a non-NULL resolvable hostname or IP address.
port must be a valid TCP port number (>0).
user may be NULL or a valid username depending on server configuration (username optional).
password should be a valid password string when authentication is required.
timeout is in milliseconds; 0 indicates a default or no explicit timeout depending on implementation.

functions.name: esl_connect
functions.signature: esl_status_t esl_connect(esl_handle_t *handle, const char *host, esl_port_t port, const char *user, const char *password);
functions.description: Connects an ESL handle to a FreeSWITCH event socket at the given host/port and authenticates using the provided user/password. This name is a macro alias for esl_connect_timeout(..., 0). Typical usage: allocate/initialize an esl_handle_t, then call esl_connect to establish the connection and perform authentication. Returns an esl_status_t indicating success or failure.
requirements: handle must be a valid, non-NULL pointer to esl_handle_t
host must be a non-NULL, NUL-terminated string
port must be of type esl_port_t; must represent a valid listening port for the target server (inferred)
user may be NULL if username is optional per server configuration (per comment: username optional)
password must be provided as a non-NULL, NUL-terminated string if the server requires authentication (inferred from purpose)
Network connectivity to host:port must be available for the call to succeed (inferred from purpose)

functions.name: esl_disconnect
functions.description: Disconnects and cleans up an ESL handle’s connection to the server.
requirements: handle must be a valid esl_handle_t pointer; safe to call when connected to terminate the connection.

functions.name: esl_send
functions.description: Sends a raw command string over the ESL connection and does not wait for a response.
requirements: handle must refer to a connected ESL session.
cmd must be a non-NULL command string understood by the server.

functions.name: esl_recv_event
functions.description: Polls the handle’s socket until an event arrives or a connection error occurs. Optionally returns the received event via save_event.
requirements: handle must refer to a connected ESL session.
check_q set to 1 makes the function check the internal queue (handle->race_event) first and return the last queued event if present.
If save_event is not NULL, it will receive a pointer to the received event; ownership/lifecycle requirements are not documented here and depend on esl_event_t semantics.

functions.name: esl_recv_event_timed
functions.signature: esl_status_t esl_recv_event_timed(esl_handle_t *handle, uint32_t ms, int check_q, esl_event_t **save_event);
functions.description: Like esl_recv_event, but returns if no event arrives within the specified timeout in milliseconds.
requirements: handle must refer to a connected ESL session.
ms is the maximum time in milliseconds to wait for an event.
check_q behaves as in esl_recv_event.
If save_event is not NULL, it will receive a pointer to the received event; ownership semantics are not specified in this header.

functions.name: esl_send_recv_timed
functions.signature: esl_status_t esl_send_recv_timed(esl_handle_t *handle, const char *cmd, uint32_t ms);
functions.description: Sends a raw command and waits for the corresponding response event or timeout. Response is stored in handle->last_sr_event and handle->last_sr_reply.
requirements: handle must refer to a connected ESL session.
cmd must be a non-NULL command string.
ms is the maximum time in milliseconds to wait for a response; 0 may indicate a default/no timeout depending on implementation.
Caller should inspect handle->last_sr_event and handle->last_sr_reply after success.

functions.name: esl_send_recv
functions.description: Sends a raw command on the connected ESL handle and waits for the corresponding response, storing it in handle->last_sr_event and handle->last_sr_reply. This name is a macro alias for esl_send_recv_timed(handle, cmd, 0). Use this when you want a synchronous request/response exchange without a custom timeout.
requirements: handle must be a valid, non-NULL pointer to an esl_handle_t
handle must be connected before calling (inferred from purpose)
cmd must be a non-NULL, NUL-terminated string containing a valid ESL command
Caller should inspect the return esl_status_t to determine success or failure and may read handle->last_sr_event or handle->last_sr_reply after a successful call (per comment)

functions.name: esl_filter
functions.signature: esl_status_t esl_filter(esl_handle_t *handle, const char *header, const char *value);
functions.description: Applies a server-side event filter for subsequent received events based on a header/value pair.
requirements: handle must refer to a connected ESL session.
header must be a non-NULL header name to filter on.
value must be a non-NULL value for the given header.

functions.name: esl_events
functions.signature: esl_status_t esl_events(esl_handle_t *handle, esl_event_type_t etype, const char *value);
functions.description: Subscribes to events from the server with a particular event serialization type (plain, XML, JSON) and event selection value.
requirements: handle must refer to a connected ESL session.
etype must be a valid esl_event_type_t (ESL_EVENT_TYPE_PLAIN, ESL_EVENT_TYPE_XML, or ESL_EVENT_TYPE_JSON).
value must specify which events to subscribe to (e.g., ‘all’, a specific event name, etc.).

functions.name: esl_wait_sock
functions.signature: int esl_wait_sock(esl_socket_t sock, uint32_t ms, esl_poll_t flags);
functions.description: Waits for I/O readiness on a socket for up to ms milliseconds according to the specified poll flags (read, write, error).
requirements: sock must be a valid socket descriptor.
ms is a timeout in milliseconds.
flags must be a bitwise OR of esl_poll_t values (ESL_POLL_READ, ESL_POLL_WRITE, ESL_POLL_ERROR).
Caller must interpret the return value according to implementation (e.g., readiness, timeout, or error).

functions.name: esl_separate_string_string
functions.signature: unsigned int esl_separate_string_string(char *buf, const char *delim, char **array, unsigned int arraylen);
functions.description: Splits the buffer string in-place using the delimiter string and stores pointers to tokens in array, up to arraylen entries. Returns the number of tokens.
requirements: buf must be a writable, NUL-terminated string; it may be modified (delimiters replaced with NULs).
delim must be a non-NULL delimiter string.
array must be a valid pointer to an array of char* with capacity arraylen.
arraylen must be > 0 to store any tokens.

functions.name: esl_recv
functions.description: Polls the handle’s socket until an event is received or a connection error occurs. This name is a macro alias for esl_recv_event(handle, 0, NULL). Use this to block until the next event arrives; the event is stored internally on the handle (e.g., handle->last_event) since no save_event is provided.
requirements: handle must be a valid, non-NULL pointer to an esl_handle_t
handle must be connected before calling (inferred from purpose)
Caller must check the returned esl_status_t for ESL_SUCCESS or an error/disconnect condition

functions.name: esl_recv_timed
functions.description: Polls the handle’s socket until an event is received, a connection error occurs, or the specified timeout (ms) elapses. This name is a macro alias for esl_recv_event_timed(handle, ms, 0, NULL). Use this to wait for an event with a maximum wait time; the event is stored internally on the handle since no save_event is provided.
requirements: handle must be a valid, non-NULL pointer to an esl_handle_t
handle must be connected before calling (inferred from purpose)
ms is a timeout in milliseconds
Caller must check the returned esl_status_t for ESL_SUCCESS, ESL_DISCONNECTED, ESL_FAIL, or timeout-related status

functions.name: esl_safe_strcasecmp
functions.signature: static inline int esl_safe_strcasecmp(const char *s1, const char *s2);
functions.description: Null-safe case-insensitive string compare. Returns 0 if strings are equal ignoring case; returns 1 if either input is NULL; otherwise defers to strcasecmp.
requirements: s1 and s2 may be NULL; if either is NULL the function returns 1.
When both s1 and s2 are non-NULL, they must be NUL-terminated C-strings.

functions.name: esl_event_create_subclass
functions.signature: ESL_DECLARE(esl_status_t) esl_event_create_subclass(esl_event_t **event, esl_event_types_t event_id, const char *subclass_name);
functions.description: Create a new event instance. For custom events (event_id == ESL_EVENT_CUSTOM), subclass_name specifies the event subclass; for non-custom events it should be NULL (ESL_EVENT_SUBCLASS_ANY). The created event must later be destroyed by the caller.
requirements: event must point to a NULL esl_event_t* on entry (the function will allocate and assign)
If event_id is not ESL_EVENT_CUSTOM, subclass_name must be NULL (ESL_EVENT_SUBCLASS_ANY)
Caller must check the return value for ESL_SUCCESS before using *event
The resulting event must be released with esl_event_destroy()

functions.name: esl_event_set_priority
functions.description: Set the priority of an existing event to the specified esl_priority_t value.
requirements: event must be a valid, initialized esl_event_t pointer
Caller should check the return value for ESL_SUCCESS

functions.name: esl_event_get_header_ptr
functions.description: Retrieve a pointer to the internal header structure for the named header in the event. Useful when the caller needs access to metadata such as array entries or indexing.
requirements: event must be a valid, initialized esl_event_t pointer
header_name must be a non-NULL header name string
Return may be NULL if the header is not present; caller must handle NULL
The returned pointer refers to internal storage owned by the event; do not free or modify it unless the API specifies otherwise (not documented here)

functions.name: esl_event_get_header_idx
functions.signature: ESL_DECLARE(char *) esl_event_get_header_idx(esl_event_t *event, const char *header_name, int idx);
functions.description: Retrieve the value of the named header from the event. If the header is an array, idx selects a specific element; otherwise idx of -1 returns the default/last value.
requirements: event must be a valid, initialized esl_event_t pointer
header_name must be a non-NULL header name string

functions.name: esl_event_get_body

Return may be NULL; caller must handle NULL

functions.name: esl_event_add_header

header_name must be a non-NULL header name string
fmt must be a valid printf-style format string, and the varargs must match fmt
stack must be one of esl_stack_t (e.g., ESL_STACK_TOP or ESL_STACK_BOTTOM)
Caller should check the return value for ESL_SUCCESS

functions.name: esl_event_add_array
functions.signature: ESL_DECLARE(int) esl_event_add_array(esl_event_t *event, const char *var, const char *val);
functions.description: Add an array element to a header identified by var, associating it with value val. Details of indexing and behavior are not documented here; inferred from name and structure.
requirements: event must be a valid, initialized esl_event_t pointer
var must be a non-NULL header name string
val may be NULL or non-NULL (behavior for NULL not documented; unknown)
Caller should check the integer return code (semantics not documented; unknown)

functions.name: esl_event_add_header_string
functions.signature: ESL_DECLARE(esl_status_t) esl_event_add_header_string(esl_event_t *event, esl_stack_t stack, const char *header_name, const char *data);
functions.description: Add a header with the given string value to the event. The header is placed at the top or bottom depending on the stack parameter.
requirements: event must be a valid, initialized esl_event_t pointer
header_name must be a non-NULL header name string
data must be a string pointer; NULL handling is not documented (unknown)
stack must be one of esl_stack_t
Caller should check the return value for ESL_SUCCESS

functions.name: esl_event_del_header_val
functions.signature: ESL_DECLARE(esl_status_t) esl_event_del_header_val(esl_event_t *event, const char *header_name, const char *var);
functions.description: Delete a header (or a specific array element of a header) from the event. When var is NULL, this behaves like deleting the header by name, as used by the esl_event_del_header macro.
requirements: event must be a valid, initialized esl_event_t pointer
header_name must be a non-NULL header name string
If var is NULL, delete the header by name; if non-NULL, delete a specific array value (exact behavior not documented)
Caller should check the return value for ESL_SUCCESS

functions.name: esl_event_destroy
functions.description: Destroy an event and free its associated resources. The function takes a pointer to the event pointer and will destroy and typically null it.
requirements: event must be a non-NULL pointer to an esl_event_t* that was created/obtained from this API
After destruction, the event pointer should not be used
It is safe to wrap with esl_event_safe_destroy macro to guard NULL

functions.name: esl_event_dup
functions.description: Duplicate an existing event into a new event object.
requirements: event must point to a NULL esl_event_t* on entry (the function will allocate and assign)
todup must be a valid, initialized esl_event_t pointer
Caller should check the return value for ESL_SUCCESS
The duplicated event must be released with esl_event_destroy()

functions.name: esl_event_merge
functions.description: Merge the contents of tomerge into event. Exact merge semantics (e.g., header conflict resolution) are not documented in this header and thus are unknown.
requirements: event must be a valid, initialized esl_event_t pointer to receive merged data
tomerge must be a valid, initialized esl_event_t pointer
Post-merge ownership/lifetime of tomerge is not specified here (unknown)

functions.name: esl_event_name
functions.description: Return the string name corresponding to an esl_event_types_t value.
requirements: Input must be a valid esl_event_types_t enumeration value
Return is a const char* owned by the library; do not modify or free

functions.name: esl_name_event
functions.description: Look up an event enumeration value by its string name and store it in type. Returns ESL_SUCCESS if name matches a known event.
requirements: name must be a non-NULL, zero-terminated string
type must be a non-NULL pointer to receive the result
Caller should check the return value for ESL_SUCCESS before using *type

functions.name: esl_event_serialize
functions.description: Serialize an event into a printable/transportable string. If encode is true, header values are URL-encoded. The function allocates the output string and assigns it to *str; the caller must free the string when done.
requirements: event must be a valid, initialized esl_event_t pointer
str must be a non-NULL pointer to char*; on success, *str will point to allocated memory that the caller must free
Caller should check the return value for ESL_SUCCESS before using *str
If encode is true, headers are URL-encoded; caller should expect encoded values

functions.name: esl_event_serialize_json
functions.description: Serialize an event into a JSON string representation. The function allocates the output string and assigns it to *str; the caller must free the string when done.
requirements: event must be a valid, initialized esl_event_t pointer
str must be a non-NULL pointer to char*; on success, *str will point to allocated memory that the caller must free
Caller should check the return value for ESL_SUCCESS before using *str

functions.name: esl_event_create_json
functions.description: Create an event from a JSON string representation.
requirements: event must point to a NULL esl_event_t* on entry (the function will allocate and assign)
json must be a non-NULL, well-formed JSON string matching the expected event schema (details not documented here)
Caller should check the return value for ESL_SUCCESS
The created event must be released with esl_event_destroy()

functions.name: esl_event_add_body
functions.description: Add a formatted body to the event using a printf-style format string and varargs. Note: the body may be shadowed by esl_event_reserve_subclass_detailed (not defined in this header).
requirements: event must be a valid, initialized esl_event_t pointer
fmt must be a valid printf-style format string, and the varargs must match fmt
Caller should check the return value for ESL_SUCCESS

functions.name: esl_event_set_body
functions.description: Set the body of the event to the provided string. Ownership semantics (copy vs. reference) are not documented here.
requirements: event must be a valid, initialized esl_event_t pointer
body may be NULL or non-NULL (exact behavior for NULL is not documented; unknown)
Caller should check the return value for ESL_SUCCESS

functions.name: esl_priority_name
functions.description: Return the string name for a given esl_priority_t value.
requirements: Input must be a valid esl_priority_t enumeration value
Return is a const char* owned by the library; do not modify or free

functions.name: esl_event_get_header
functions.description: Macro wrapper for esl_event_get_header_idx(event, header_name, -1). Retrieves the value of the specified header from an event, returning a pointer to the value for the last/only occurrence. Use when you want a single header value without indexing.
requirements: event must be a valid, initialized esl_event_t pointer
header_name must be a non-NULL, NUL-terminated string
The returned char* points to internal storage; ownership is unknown from this header—do not free or modify it unless the library explicitly documents that it is safe
If the header is not present, the function may return NULL—callers must handle a NULL return

functions.name: esl_event_del_header
functions.description: Macro wrapper for esl_event_del_header_val(event, header_name, NULL). Deletes the specified header from an event. Using the macro form removes the header entirely (all values/occurrences).
requirements: event must be a valid, initialized esl_event_t pointer
header_name must be a non-NULL, NUL-terminated string
Callers must check the returned esl_status_t to determine success or failure
If multiple values exist for the header, this macro form removes the header entirely (per its expansion to esl_event_del_header_val with var == NULL)

functions.name: esl_event_create
functions.description: Macro wrapper for esl_event_create_subclass(event, id, ESL_EVENT_SUBCLASS_ANY). Creates a new event that is not a custom event (no subclass). Intended for creating standard (non-custom) events.
requirements: event must be a valid pointer to an esl_event_t* variable that is currently NULL (per comment: "a NULL pointer on which to create the event")
id must be a valid esl_event_types_t and should not be ESL_EVENT_CUSTOM (macro is for non-custom events)
On success, *event will point to a newly created event; callers are responsible for eventually destroying it with esl_event_destroy or esl_event_safe_destroy
Callers must check the returned esl_status_t for success before using *event

functions.name: esl_event_safe_destroy
functions.description: Macro that conditionally destroys an event: if (event) esl_event_destroy(event). Safe helper to destroy an event object when the pointer-to-pointer itself may be NULL. Calls esl_event_destroy to free the event and associated resources.
requirements: event may be NULL; if NULL, the macro performs no action
If non-NULL, event must point to an esl_event_t* previously created by this API
After destruction, the underlying esl_event_destroy will release resources; callers must not use the destroyed event pointer thereafter
This is a macro and may evaluate its argument more than once; pass a simple variable (not an expression with side effects)

functions.name: esl_buffer_create
functions.signature: ESL_DECLARE(esl_status_t) esl_buffer_create(esl_buffer_t **buffer, esl_size_t blocksize, esl_size_t start_len, esl_size_t max_len);
functions.description: Allocate a new dynamic esl_buffer. Callers provide an out-parameter to receive the created buffer, a blocksize used for growth, an initial reserved size, and a maximum size cap. Use when you need a resizable read/write buffer managed by this API.
requirements: buffer must be a valid, writable pointer to an esl_buffer_t* (out-parameter)
blocksize, start_len, and max_len are size values; exact constraints are not documented here
Behavior when start_len > max_len is not documented
Returns an esl_status_t indicating success/failure; exact status codes are not documented

functions.name: esl_buffer_len
functions.description: Return the total length (capacity) of the buffer object.
requirements: buffer must be a valid esl_buffer_t*

functions.name: esl_buffer_freespace
functions.description: Return the amount of free space currently available in the buffer.
requirements: buffer must be a valid esl_buffer_t*

functions.name: esl_buffer_inuse
functions.description: Return how many bytes of the buffer are currently in use (occupied with data).
requirements: buffer must be a valid esl_buffer_t*

functions.name: esl_buffer_read
functions.description: Read up to datalen bytes from the buffer if available and remove the read data from the buffer. Returns the number of bytes actually read.
requirements: buffer must be a valid esl_buffer_t*
data must point to a writable memory region of at least datalen bytes
datalen is the maximum number of bytes to read

functions.name: esl_buffer_read_packet
functions.description: Read a single packet from the buffer, up to maxlen bytes. Returns the number of bytes actually read. Details of packet framing are not documented in this header and are unknown.
requirements: buffer must be a valid esl_buffer_t*
data must point to a writable memory region of at least maxlen bytes
maxlen limits the maximum bytes copied for one packet
Packet structure/framing requirements are unknown from this header

functions.name: esl_buffer_packet_count
functions.description: Return the number of packets currently queued in the buffer. The definition of a packet is not documented in this header and is unknown.
requirements: buffer must be a valid esl_buffer_t*

functions.name: esl_buffer_read_loop
functions.description: Read data from the buffer in a looping fashion. Once you have read all data from the buffer it will loop around, allowing continuous reading according to the loop count set via esl_buffer_set_loops. Returns the number of bytes actually read.
requirements: buffer must be a valid esl_buffer_t*
data must point to a writable memory region of at least datalen bytes
datalen is the maximum number of bytes to read per call
Loop count behavior is controlled by esl_buffer_set_loops; exact stopping conditions beyond the note are not fully documented

functions.name: esl_buffer_set_loops
functions.description: Set the number of loops used by esl_buffer_read_loop. A value of -1 indicates infinite looping.
requirements: buffer must be a valid esl_buffer_t*
loops controls looping count; -1 means infinite; other value semantics beyond this are not documented

functions.name: esl_buffer_write
functions.signature: ESL_DECLARE(esl_size_t) esl_buffer_write(esl_buffer_t *buffer, const void *data, esl_size_t datalen);
functions.description: Write up to datalen bytes into the buffer. Returns the amount of buffer used after the write, or 0 if no space is available. Buffer growth may be bounded by max_len set at creation.
requirements: buffer must be a valid esl_buffer_t*
data must point to a readable memory region of at least datalen bytes
If no space is available, the function returns 0
Exact behavior when datalen exceeds available space (partial writes vs. failure) is not fully documented

functions.name: esl_buffer_toss
functions.description: Remove datalen bytes of data from the buffer. Returns the size of the buffer after the operation, or 0 if unable to remove that much data.
requirements: buffer must be a valid esl_buffer_t*
datalen should not exceed the amount of data available; otherwise the function returns 0

functions.name: esl_buffer_zero
functions.description: Remove all data from the buffer (reset usage to empty).
requirements: buffer must be a valid esl_buffer_t*

functions.name: esl_buffer_destroy
functions.description: Destroy a buffer created dynamically. No-op for pooled buffers. Use to release resources when done with a dynamic esl_buffer.
requirements: buffer must be a valid, writable pointer to an esl_buffer_t*
Only necessary for dynamic buffers; it is a no-op on pooled ones
Post-conditions (e.g., whether *buffer is set to NULL) are not documented

functions.name: esl_buffer_seek
functions.description: Seek to an offset from the beginning of the buffer. Returns the new position.
requirements: buffer must be a valid esl_buffer_t*
datalen is the byte offset to seek to; valid range and behavior when out-of-bounds are not documented

functions.name: esl_buffer_zwrite
functions.signature: ESL_DECLARE(esl_size_t) esl_buffer_zwrite(esl_buffer_t *buffer, const void *data, esl_size_t datalen);
functions.description: Write variant for the buffer. The exact semantics of zwrite (e.g., zero-termination or zero-fill) are not documented in this header and are unknown. Likely writes up to datalen bytes and returns a size value similar to esl_buffer_write.
requirements: buffer must be a valid esl_buffer_t*
data must point to a readable memory region of at least datalen bytes
Exact differences from esl_buffer_write are unknown from this header

functions.name: cJSON_GetObjectCstr
functions.description: Returns the C string value associated with the given key in a cJSON object. Intended as a convenience accessor that looks up an item by name and returns its string value (or NULL if not found/not a string). Details are inferred from the name; the header provides no implementation or comments.
requirements: object must point to a valid cJSON node that represents an object (inferred from function name and cJSON API patterns).
string must be a non-NULL key name (inferred).
The returned pointer, if non-NULL, is expected to be owned by the cJSON tree; the caller must not free or modify it, and its lifetime is tied to the cJSON document (inferred).
If the key is absent or the item is not a string, the function may return NULL; callers should check for NULL (inferred).

functions.name: esl_json_add_child_obj
functions.signature: static inline cJSON *esl_json_add_child_obj(cJSON *json, const char *name, cJSON *obj);
functions.description: Adds a child object to the given cJSON object under the provided name. If obj is non-NULL, it is inserted; otherwise a new empty object is created and inserted. Returns the inserted object node.
requirements: json must be non-NULL (enforced via esl_assert).
If obj is NULL, memory allocation is performed via cJSON_CreateObject; allocation failure triggers esl_assert (program abort).
name should be a valid key string for an object (inferred).
json should be a cJSON object (not an array/value) suitable for cJSON_AddItemToObject (inferred from cJSON API).
If a non-NULL obj is passed, it should be a standalone cJSON object node not already attached to another tree (inferred from cJSON_AddItemToObject semantics).
After insertion, ownership of the returned node is transferred to json; the caller must not free it independently (inferred from cJSON API).

functions.name: esl_json_add_child_array
functions.description: Creates a new empty cJSON array and adds it as a child of the given cJSON object under the provided name. Returns the created array node.
requirements: json must be non-NULL (enforced via esl_assert).
Memory allocation is performed via cJSON_CreateArray; allocation failure triggers esl_assert (program abort).
name should be a valid key string for an object (inferred).
json should be a cJSON object (not an array/value) suitable for cJSON_AddItemToObject (inferred from cJSON API).
After insertion, ownership of the returned array node is transferred to json; the caller must not free it independently (inferred from cJSON API).

functions.name: esl_json_add_child_string
functions.signature: static inline cJSON *esl_json_add_child_string(cJSON *json, const char *name, const char *val);
functions.description: Creates a new cJSON string node with the given value and adds it as a child of the given cJSON object under the provided name. Returns the created string node.
requirements: json must be non-NULL (enforced via esl_assert).
Memory allocation is performed via cJSON_CreateString; allocation failure triggers esl_assert (program abort).
val should be a non-NULL C string suitable for cJSON_CreateString (inferred from cJSON API).
name should be a valid key string for an object (inferred).
json should be a cJSON object (not an array/value) suitable for cJSON_AddItemToObject (inferred from cJSON API).
After insertion, ownership of the returned string node is transferred to json; the caller must not free it independently (inferred from cJSON API).

functions.name: cJSON_Version
functions.description: Returns the cJSON library version as a null-terminated string literal. Useful for logging or feature checks.
requirements: No arguments required.
Return value is a pointer to a string that must not be freed by the caller.

functions.name: cJSON_InitHooks
functions.description: Installs custom memory allocation hooks (malloc/free) for cJSON. Call before any other cJSON allocation to affect all subsequent operations.
requirements: hooks may be NULL to reset to defaults (implied by typical usage; not explicitly stated).
If hooks is non-NULL, hooks->malloc_fn and hooks->free_fn should be compatible with malloc(size_t) and free(void*), and callable for the process lifetime.
On Windows, functions should use CDECL calling convention (per comment).
Must be called before using functions that allocate/free cJSON items to ensure consistent allocator usage.

functions.name: cJSON_Parse
functions.description: Parses a null-terminated UTF-8 JSON text into a cJSON tree. On success returns the root cJSON; on failure returns NULL. Caller owns the returned tree and must free it with cJSON_Delete.
requirements: value must be a valid pointer to a null-terminated JSON string.
On success, caller must call cJSON_Delete on the returned cJSON* to free all memory.
On failure, use cJSON_GetErrorPtr to locate the parse error.

functions.name: cJSON_ParseWithOpts
functions.signature: cJSON * cJSON_ParseWithOpts(const char *value, const char **return_parse_end, cJSON_bool require_null_terminated);
functions.description: Parses JSON with options. If require_null_terminated is nonzero, the input must end right after the parsed JSON (no trailing chars). If return_parse_end is non-NULL, it receives a pointer to the position where parsing stopped (or the error location on failure). Returns root cJSON on success, NULL on failure.
requirements: value must point to a valid JSON buffer; if require_null_terminated is true, value must be null-terminated and contain no trailing non-whitespace after the JSON.
If return_parse_end is non-NULL, it must be a valid pointer to receive the end pointer; on failure it points to the error position consistent with cJSON_GetErrorPtr.
Caller must call cJSON_Delete on non-NULL return.

functions.name: cJSON_Print
functions.description: Serializes a cJSON tree to a newly allocated, formatted JSON string. The string is pretty-printed. Caller must free the returned buffer using the same allocator configured for cJSON (stdlib free, hooks->free_fn, or cJSON_free).
requirements: item must be a valid cJSON pointer.
Caller must free the returned char* using stdlib free, cJSON_Hooks.free_fn, or cJSON_free as appropriate for the configured allocator.
Returns NULL on failure (e.g., allocation failure).

functions.name: cJSON_PrintUnformatted
functions.description: Serializes a cJSON tree to a newly allocated, minified (no whitespace) JSON string. Caller must free the returned buffer with the allocator consistent with cJSON.
requirements: item must be a valid cJSON pointer.
Caller must free the returned buffer using stdlib free, cJSON_Hooks.free_fn, or cJSON_free, matching the configured allocator.
Returns NULL on failure.

functions.name: cJSON_PrintBuffered
functions.signature: char * cJSON_PrintBuffered(const cJSON *item, int prebuffer, cJSON_bool fmt);
functions.description: Serializes a cJSON tree using a buffered strategy. prebuffer is an initial size guess to reduce reallocations. If fmt is nonzero, pretty-printed output is produced, otherwise unformatted. Returns newly allocated string to be freed by caller.
requirements: item must be a valid cJSON pointer.
prebuffer should be a non-negative integer; larger values may reduce reallocations.
Caller must free the returned buffer using the allocator consistent with cJSON configuration.
Returns NULL on failure.

functions.name: cJSON_PrintPreallocated
functions.signature: cJSON_bool cJSON_PrintPreallocated(cJSON *item, char *buffer, const int length, const cJSON_bool format);
functions.description: Serializes a cJSON tree into a caller-provided buffer of given length. Returns 1 on success, 0 on failure. If format is nonzero, output is pretty-printed. The caller fully manages the buffer lifecycle.
requirements: item must be a valid cJSON pointer.
buffer must be a valid, writable memory region of at least length bytes.
Length must be sufficient; implementation may underestimate needs, so the header notes to allocate 5 extra bytes beyond the expected size to be safe.
Caller must not free via cJSON; this function does not allocate the output buffer.
On failure, return value is 0; buffer contents may be incomplete.

functions.name: cJSON_Delete
functions.description: Deletes a cJSON item and all of its sub-items, freeing memory according to the configured allocator.
requirements: c may be NULL (typical behavior is no-op; not explicitly stated).
All cJSON trees obtained from parse/create functions must be freed with cJSON_Delete unless ownership has been transferred/detached.
Do not use the cJSON pointer or any of its children after deletion.

functions.name: cJSON_GetArraySize
functions.description: Returns the number of items in a cJSON array or object. For arrays, it's the element count; for objects, the number of key/value pairs.
requirements: array must point to a cJSON of type cJSON_Array or cJSON_Object for meaningful results.
Returns 0 for empty arrays/objects or possibly for invalid input.

functions.name: cJSON_GetArrayItem
functions.description: Retrieves the element at zero-based index from a cJSON array. Returns NULL if index is out of range or on error.
requirements: array must be a cJSON of type cJSON_Array.
index should be >= 0 and less than the array size.
Returned pointer is owned by the array; do not free it independently.

functions.name: cJSON_GetObjectItem
functions.signature: cJSON * cJSON_GetObjectItem(const cJSON * const object, const char * const string);
functions.description: Finds a member of a cJSON object by key, case-insensitive. Returns the matching item or NULL if not found.
requirements: object must be a cJSON of type cJSON_Object.
string must be a non-NULL null-terminated key string.
Returned pointer is owned by the object; do not free it.

functions.name: cJSON_GetObjectItemCaseSensitive
functions.signature: cJSON * cJSON_GetObjectItemCaseSensitive(const cJSON * const object, const char * const string);
functions.description: Finds a member of a cJSON object by key, case-sensitive. Returns the matching item or NULL if not found.
requirements: object must be a cJSON of type cJSON_Object.
string must be a non-NULL null-terminated key string.
Returned pointer is owned by the object; do not free it.

functions.name: cJSON_HasObjectItem
functions.description: Checks whether a cJSON object contains a key. Likely case-sensitive/insensitive behavior follows GetObjectItem? Not explicitly stated; inferred typical behavior is case-sensitive counterpart may exist. Returns 1 if present, 0 otherwise.
requirements: object must be a cJSON of type cJSON_Object.
string must be a non-NULL null-terminated key string.

functions.name: cJSON_GetErrorPtr
functions.description: For failed parses, returns a pointer into the input where the error occurred. Returns NULL (0) when cJSON_Parse succeeds. Useful for diagnostics.
requirements: Call after a parse attempt to get error location; pointer is into the original input buffer, which must remain valid to interpret it.
Do not free the returned pointer.

functions.name: cJSON_GetStringValue
functions.description: If item is a string, returns its valuestring; otherwise returns NULL. Allows quick type-check and access.
requirements: item must be a valid cJSON pointer.
Do not modify or free the returned string; its lifetime is managed by the cJSON item.

functions.name: cJSON_IsInvalid
functions.description: Returns nonzero if the item is of type cJSON_Invalid. Type-check helper.
requirements: item must be a valid cJSON pointer (may be NULL; in comparison helpers, NULL is considered invalid in some contexts per comments).

functions.name: cJSON_IsFalse
functions.description: Returns nonzero if the item is the JSON literal false.
requirements: item must be a valid cJSON pointer.

functions.name: cJSON_IsTrue
functions.description: Returns nonzero if the item is the JSON literal true.
requirements: item must be a valid cJSON pointer.

functions.name: cJSON_IsBool
functions.description: Returns nonzero if the item is a JSON boolean (true or false).
requirements: item must be a valid cJSON pointer.

functions.name: cJSON_IsNull
functions.description: Returns nonzero if the item is the JSON literal null.
requirements: item must be a valid cJSON pointer.

functions.name: cJSON_IsNumber
functions.description: Returns nonzero if the item is a JSON number.
requirements: item must be a valid cJSON pointer.

functions.name: cJSON_IsString
functions.description: Returns nonzero if the item is a JSON string.
requirements: item must be a valid cJSON pointer.

functions.name: cJSON_IsArray
functions.description: Returns nonzero if the item is a JSON array.
requirements: item must be a valid cJSON pointer.

functions.name: cJSON_IsObject
functions.description: Returns nonzero if the item is a JSON object.
requirements: item must be a valid cJSON pointer.

functions.name: cJSON_IsRaw
functions.description: Returns nonzero if the item is a raw JSON chunk (cJSON_Raw), which stores uninterpreted JSON text.

functions.name: cJSON_CreateNull
functions.description: Creates a new cJSON item representing the JSON literal null.
requirements: Returns NULL on allocation failure.
Caller owns the item and must free it with cJSON_Delete or attach it to a parent that will be deleted.

functions.name: cJSON_CreateTrue
functions.description: Creates a new cJSON item representing the JSON literal true.
requirements: Returns NULL on allocation failure.
Caller must eventually free via cJSON_Delete or by deleting a parent containing it.

functions.name: cJSON_CreateFalse
functions.description: Creates a new cJSON item representing the JSON literal false.
requirements: Returns NULL on allocation failure.
Caller must eventually free via cJSON_Delete or by deleting a parent containing it.

functions.name: cJSON_CreateBool
functions.description: Creates a new cJSON boolean item with the given boolean value.
requirements: Returns NULL on allocation failure.
Caller must eventually free via cJSON_Delete or by deleting a parent containing it.

functions.name: cJSON_CreateNumber
functions.description: Creates a new cJSON number item with the given double value.
requirements: Returns NULL on allocation failure.

functions.name: cJSON_CreateString
functions.description: Creates a new cJSON string item by copying the provided C string.
requirements: string must be a non-NULL null-terminated string (implied by typical behavior).
Returns NULL on allocation failure.
Caller must eventually free the item.

functions.name: cJSON_CreateRaw
functions.description: Creates a new cJSON raw item that stores provided raw JSON text as-is.

Callers must check the returned esl_status_t to determine success or failure.
The thread is detached; callers must not attempt to join it.

Should be called before thread creation calls that rely on the default stack size to ensure the override takes effect.

functions.name: esl_mutex_create
functions.description: Allocates and initializes a new mutex and stores it in *mutex. Use with esl_mutex_lock/trylock/unlock for mutual exclusion. Returns an esl_status_t indicating success or failure.
requirements: mutex must be a non-null pointer to an esl_mutex_t* storage location.
*mutex must be writable; on success it will be set to a valid, initialized mutex object.
Callers must check the returned esl_status_t to determine success or failure.
A successfully created mutex must be destroyed with esl_mutex_destroy when no longer needed.

functions.name: esl_mutex_destroy
functions.description: Destroys a previously created mutex and releases its resources. On success, the mutex becomes invalid for further use. The function returns an esl_status_t status code.
requirements: mutex must be a non-null pointer to an esl_mutex_t* previously set by esl_mutex_create.
The mutex must not be locked by any thread at the time of destruction.
After successful destruction, the mutex must no longer be used; callers should treat *mutex as invalid (setting it to NULL is recommended if the implementation does not do so).
Callers must check the returned esl_status_t to determine success or failure.

functions.name: esl_mutex_lock
functions.description: Blocks until the specified mutex is acquired by the calling thread, providing mutual exclusion. Returns an esl_status_t indicating success or failure. Use with esl_mutex_unlock to release.
requirements: mutex must be a valid, initialized mutex obtained from esl_mutex_create.
The calling thread must not already hold the mutex unless the implementation supports recursive locking (not specified here).
Callers must check the returned esl_status_t to determine success or failure.
Must be paired with esl_mutex_unlock by the same thread on the same mutex once the protected section is complete.

functions.name: esl_mutex_trylock
functions.description: Attempts to acquire the mutex without blocking. If the mutex is already locked, returns immediately with a non-success status; otherwise locks it for the calling thread. Use esl_mutex_unlock to release on success.
requirements: mutex must be a valid, initialized mutex obtained from esl_mutex_create.
The calling thread must handle both success and the case where the mutex is already locked by another thread.
Callers must check the returned esl_status_t to determine whether the lock was acquired or an error occurred.
If successful, the calling thread must later call esl_mutex_unlock on the same mutex.

functions.name: esl_mutex_unlock
functions.description: Releases a mutex previously acquired by the calling thread via esl_mutex_lock or esl_mutex_trylock. Returns an esl_status_t indicating success or failure.
requirements: mutex must be a valid, initialized mutex obtained from esl_mutex_create.
The calling thread must currently hold the mutex; unlocking a mutex not owned by the caller is invalid.
Callers must check the returned esl_status_t to determine success or failure.
Each successful lock acquisition must be matched with exactly one unlock by the same thread.

functions.name: esl_true
functions.description: Evaluates whether a string expression represents a true value. Returns nonzero if expr matches common truthy tokens (yes, on, true, enabled, active, allow) case-insensitively, or if atoi(expr) is nonzero; otherwise returns 0. If expr is NULL, returns 0. Useful for parsing boolean-like configuration values.
requirements: expr may be NULL; if NULL the function returns 0
expr should be a null-terminated C string if non-NULL
Comparison is case-insensitive; numeric strings are evaluated via atoi

functions.name: esl_false
functions.description: Evaluates whether a string expression represents a false value. Returns nonzero if expr matches common falsy tokens (no, off, false, disabled, inactive, disallow) case-insensitively, or if atoi(expr) is zero; otherwise returns 0. If expr is NULL, returns 0. Useful for parsing boolean-like configuration values.
requirements: expr may be NULL; if NULL the function returns 0
expr should be a null-terminated C string if non-NULL
Comparison is case-insensitive; numeric strings are evaluated via atoi

functions.name: esl_config_open_file
functions.description: Opens a configuration file and initializes the provided esl_config_t handle for iteration over its contents. Returns 1 on success and 0 on failure. Intended to be called before reading name/value pairs from the file.
requirements: cfg must be a valid, non-NULL pointer to an esl_config_t that the function can initialize
file_path must be a valid, null-terminated path string referring to an accessible configuration file
Caller must check the return value and only proceed if it returns 1 (success)
After a successful open, the handle should later be closed with esl_config_close_file

functions.name: esl_config_close_file
functions.description: Closes a previously opened configuration file associated with the provided esl_config_t handle and releases any related resources. Intended to be paired with esl_config_open_file.
requirements: cfg should be a valid, non-NULL pointer to an esl_config_t
cfg should have been previously passed to and successfully opened by esl_config_open_file before closing
Caller should not use the handle for reading pairs after closing

functions.name: esl_config_next_pair
functions.description: Retrieves the next name/value pair from the opened configuration file. On success, writes pointers to the variable name and its value into var and val, and returns a nonzero value; returns 0 when no more pairs or on failure. Used to iterate through configuration entries after opening the file.
requirements: cfg must be a valid, non-NULL pointer to an esl_config_t that has been successfully opened with esl_config_open_file
var and val must be non-NULL pointers to char* locations where the function can store output pointers
Caller must check the return value to determine if a pair was retrieved
Memory ownership/lifetime of the returned strings is unknown from the header; caller should not assume they are heap-allocated

functions.name: esl_config_get_cas_bits
functions.description: Parses CAS (Channel Associated Signaling) bits from a configuration string value into outbits. The input is expected to be in the format "whatever:xxxx" where the portion after the colon encodes the bits. Return value semantics are not documented in this header and are therefore unknown.
requirements: strvalue must be a valid, null-terminated string and is expected to be in the format "whatever:xxxx"
strvalue is non-const; the function may modify it (exact behavior not documented)
outbits must be a valid, non-NULL pointer to at least one byte where the parsed CAS bits will be stored
Caller should check the integer return value, but exact success/failure conventions are unknown

functions.name: ESLevent::ESLevent
functions.description: Constructs a new ESLevent by allocating an underlying ESL event of the given type, optionally with a subclass. Used to create an event to populate and send or to manipulate locally.
requirements: this must refer to a valid object being constructed (standard C++ construction).
type must point to a valid, null-terminated C string naming a known ESL event type.
subclass_name may be NULL; if provided it must point to a valid, null-terminated C string.

functions.name: ESLevent::~ESLevent
functions.description: Destructor for ESLevent. Cleans up internal resources and, depending on ownership flags, may free the underlying esl_event_t.
requirements: The ESLevent instance must not be used after destruction.

If constructed with ownership of an underlying esl_event_t (e.g., free_me non-zero), it may free that event on destruction; callers must not free it separately (ownership semantics not fully documented here).

functions.name: ESLevent::serialize
functions.description: Serializes the event into a string representation, optionally using a specified format. Useful for logging, debugging, or sending over a connection.
requirements: this must be a valid, initialized ESLevent instance.
format may be NULL to use a default format; if provided, it must be a valid, null-terminated C string recognized by ESL (exact accepted formats unknown).
Returned pointer refers to internal storage (serialized_string); its lifetime is tied to the ESLevent object and may be invalidated by subsequent calls or destruction.

functions.name: ESLevent::setPriority
functions.description: Sets the priority of the event, influencing delivery/processing semantics in ESL. Returns success status.
requirements: this must be a valid, initialized ESLevent instance.
priority must be a valid esl_priority_t value defined by the ESL API.

functions.name: ESLevent::getHeader
functions.description: Retrieves the value of an event header by name. If multiple headers with the same name exist, idx may select a specific occurrence (indexing semantics inferred: -1 likely means first or combined; exact behavior unknown). Returns NULL if not present.
requirements: this must be a valid, initialized ESLevent instance.
header_name must be a non-null, null-terminated C string naming the header.
idx may be -1 or a non-negative index; specific range/meaning beyond that is unknown.
Returned pointer is valid while the underlying event remains unchanged; do not free it.

functions.name: ESLevent::getBody
functions.description: Returns the body/payload of the event, if any. Useful for custom event payloads or message bodies.
requirements: this must be a valid, initialized ESLevent instance.
Returned pointer may be NULL if no body is present and is owned by the event; do not free it and avoid use after the ESLevent is modified or destroyed.

functions.name: ESLevent::getType
functions.description: Returns the event type string for this event.
requirements: this must be a valid, initialized ESLevent instance.
Returned pointer is owned by the event; do not free it.

functions.name: ESLevent::addBody
functions.description: Sets or appends to the event body with the provided string value. Returns success status.
requirements: this must be a valid, initialized ESLevent instance.
value must be a non-null, null-terminated C string.

functions.name: ESLevent::addHeader
functions.description: Adds or sets a header on the event. If the header exists, behavior (overwrite vs. add) depends on ESL semantics (unknown here). Returns success status.
requirements: this must be a valid, initialized ESLevent instance.
header_name must be a non-null, null-terminated C string.
value must be a non-null, null-terminated C string.

functions.name: ESLevent::pushHeader
functions.description: Pushes a header value, supporting multiple values under the same header name by appending at the end. Returns success status.
requirements: this must be a valid, initialized ESLevent instance.
header_name must be a non-null, null-terminated C string.
value must be a non-null, null-terminated C string.

functions.name: ESLevent::unshiftHeader
functions.description: Adds a header value at the beginning of a header list when multiple values are supported. Returns success status.
requirements: this must be a valid, initialized ESLevent instance.
header_name must be a non-null, null-terminated C string.
value must be a non-null, null-terminated C string.

functions.name: ESLevent::delHeader
functions.description: Deletes all instances of the specified header from the event. Returns success status.
requirements: this must be a valid, initialized ESLevent instance.
header_name must be a non-null, null-terminated C string.

functions.name: ESLevent::firstHeader
functions.description: Begins iteration over the event's headers, returning the name of the first header. Use nextHeader() to continue iteration. Returns NULL if there are no headers.
requirements: this must be a valid, initialized ESLevent instance.
Iteration order and concurrent modification semantics are unspecified; avoid modifying headers during iteration.

functions.name: ESLevent::nextHeader
functions.description: Continues iteration over the event's headers, returning the name of the next header. Returns NULL when no further headers exist.
requirements: this must be a valid, initialized ESLevent instance.
Must be called after firstHeader() to begin iteration.
Avoid modifying headers during iteration.

functions.name: ESLconnection::ESLconnection
functions.signature: ESLconnection::ESLconnection(const char *host, const int port, const char *user, const char *password)
functions.description: Constructs a connection and attempts to connect to an ESL server at host:port using a username and password for authentication.
requirements: host must be a non-null, null-terminated C string resolvable as a hostname or IP.
port must be a valid TCP port number in range 1-65535.
user must be a non-null, null-terminated C string.
password must be a non-null, null-terminated C string.

functions.name: ESLconnection::~ESLconnection
functions.description: Destructor for ESLconnection. Closes the connection and frees associated resources as appropriate.
requirements: The ESLconnection must not be used after destruction.
If constructed from an external socket descriptor, whether the destructor closes the socket is not specified here (unknown).

functions.name: ESLconnection::socketDescriptor
functions.description: Returns the underlying socket descriptor associated with this connection, or a negative value on error/disconnected (exact error semantics unknown).
requirements: this must be a valid, initialized ESLconnection instance.

functions.name: ESLconnection::connected
functions.description: Reports whether the connection is established. Typically returns non-zero if connected, zero otherwise (exact return convention unknown).
requirements: this must be a valid, initialized ESLconnection instance.

functions.name: ESLconnection::getInfo
functions.description: Retrieves the initial connection info event, often containing channel variables or server greeting depending on ESL mode. Returns an ESLevent pointer or NULL on failure.
requirements: this must be a valid, initialized ESLconnection instance and typically should be connected.
Caller is responsible for managing the returned ESLevent per library semantics (ownership and lifetime unknown here).

functions.name: ESLconnection::send
functions.description: Sends a raw command string over the connection. Returns a status code; exact values are not documented here.
requirements: this must be a valid, connected ESLconnection instance.
cmd must be a non-null, null-terminated C string representing a complete ESL command line.

functions.name: ESLconnection::sendRecv
functions.description: Sends a raw command and waits for a reply, returning the response event. Useful for synchronous request/response operations.
requirements: this must be a valid, connected ESLconnection instance.
cmd must be a non-null, null-terminated C string.
Blocking behavior depends on network and server; may block until a response is received.

functions.name: ESLconnection::api
functions.description: Issues an 'api' command to the ESL server, optionally with an argument, and returns the response as an ESLevent.
requirements: this must be a valid, connected ESLconnection instance.
cmd must be a non-null, null-terminated C string naming the API command.
arg may be NULL; if provided it must be a null-terminated C string.
Operation is synchronous and may block until the server responds.

functions.name: ESLconnection::bgapi

functions.description: Issues a 'bgapi' (background API) command. Optionally includes an argument and job UUID. Returns an event, typically acknowledging job submission; result completion arrives asynchronously.
requirements: this must be a valid, connected ESLconnection instance.
cmd must be a non-null, null-terminated C string naming the API command.
arg may be NULL; if provided it must be a null-terminated C string.
job_uuid may be NULL; if provided it must be a null-terminated C string and should be a valid UUID string (format not enforced here).

functions.name: ESLconnection::sendEvent
functions.description: Sends an event over the connection. Returns a response/acknowledgment event or NULL on failure.
requirements: this must be a valid, connected ESLconnection instance.
send_me must be a non-null pointer to a valid ESLevent instance prepared for sending.
Ownership of send_me is not transferred unless documented elsewhere (unknown).

functions.name: ESLconnection::sendMSG
functions.description: Sends a message (often a mod_event_socket 'sendmsg') optionally targeting a specific channel UUID. Returns a status code.
requirements: this must be a valid, connected ESLconnection instance.
send_me must be a non-null pointer to a valid ESLevent representing the message.
uuid may be NULL; if provided it must be a valid, null-terminated C string representing a channel UUID.

functions.name: ESLconnection::recvEvent
functions.description: Receives the next event from the connection, blocking until one is available. Returns the event or NULL on error/disconnect.
requirements: this must be a valid, connected ESLconnection instance.

functions.name: ESLconnection::recvEventTimed
functions.description: Receives an event, waiting up to the specified timeout in milliseconds. Returns NULL if the timeout elapses or on error.

functions.name: ESLconnection::filter

header must be a non-null, null-terminated C string naming the header to filter on.
value must be a non-null, null-terminated C string.

functions.description: Subscribes to events of a specified delivery type and scope (e.g., plain, json) with a value specifying which events to receive (e.g., all, CUSTOM, specific types). Returns a status code.
requirements: this must be a valid, connected ESLconnection instance.
etype must be a non-null, null-terminated C string specifying event format/delivery (exact accepted values unknown).
